title: Cold Spicy Sichuan Noodles
author: Hao Ye
license_note: Confirmed via CrossRef DOI metadata: dx.doi.org/10.17504/protocols.io.ik4ccyw

steps.title: Prepare pickled cucumbers
steps.instruction: Make a brine with 1 cup rice vinegar (unseasoned), 1 cup water, 3/4 cup sugar, and 1 tbsp salt; place 6 julienned Persian cucumbers (cut to 2–2.5 in long pieces with a bit of peel) in the brine, let sit (can be prepared the night before). The brine is sufficient for 6 cucumbers; use 3–4 cucumbers per 12 oz noodles and reserve the rest.

steps.title: Cook and cool noodles
steps.instruction: Boil approximately 12 oz noodles according to package instructions; after cooking, rinse the noodles under cold water to cool them, then drain.

steps.title: Combine noodles with oil and cucumbers
steps.instruction: While the noodles are still warm, toss them with 2 tbsp sesame seed oil and the prepared pickled cucumbers to prevent sticking; cover and chill in the refrigerator while the sauce is prepared.

steps.title: Make spicy sauce
steps.instruction: In a bowl, mix together vinegar, peppercorn oil, and pickled peppers (quantities as desired); stir well to ensure the oil and vinegar are fully emulsified before tasting.

steps.title: Assemble dish and serve
steps.instruction: Remove chilled noodles and sauce from the fridge, let them sit at room temperature for about 5 minutes, then thoroughly combine the sauce with the noodles; top with thinly sliced green onions (2 bunches), cover, and serve immediately. Noodles and sauce can be stored separately in the fridge for about one day.
